proof.criterion: Review round 3, item 1. Three comments stated the causality backwards: they said a fatal advice failure drops the suggestions a creation had already computed and persisted. It does not, and the sentence an agent reads to learn what the server does must say the true reason.
proof.surface: The code the comments describe, read at the lines the reviewer named: `issue_create.go`, `asks.go`, and the three places the sentence appears.
proof.command: `sed -n '398,412p' packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_create.go` and `sed -n '294,305p' packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/asks.go`, read before the thread landed; then the three edits.
proof.observed: `issue_create.go` calls `computeAndPersistSuggestions` only inside `if advice != nil`, after the advice is built, so a fatal advice failure there meant the suggestions were never computed and no row was ever written — the tolerance this change adds is worth more than the old sentence claimed, not less. The 'already computed and persisted' framing belongs to the ask path, where `asks.go` computes them first and falls back to `withRawAdvice(ask, suggestionsOnlyAdvice{…})`, the fallback `TestCreateAskOnIssueKeepsSuggestionsWhenWriteAdviceFails` guards. All three places now say that: `packages/envoy/AGENTS.md`, the doc comment on `legionManagedStatusAdvice` (`write_advice.go`), and the comment on `TestWriteAdviceKeepsItsFieldsWhenTheLegionWalkFails` (`write_advice_test.go`), with the ask path named in `AGENTS.md` as the contrast so the two are not confused again.

No behaviour changed: the whole `internal/dispatch/api` and `model` suites pass unchanged, and the acceptance criteria answer exactly as they did at the previous head.

The Go suite's Postgres is initialised with `--locale-provider=icu --icu-locale=en-US` rather than the plan's `--locale=C`, because the api package's rank test refuses a byte-order database (rank_test.go:317).
discoveredComplexity: Refused by the architect and recorded rather than deferred, so no one re-opens them as findings: moving the claim-side walk onto the pool (it would read the answer without the issue's row held, which is the property the design asks for) and collapsing the two savepoint wrappers into one (tidiness over correct, tested code in the function this issue took three review rounds to settle). Neither is implemented and neither is filed.
`legion_managed_status` is absent in four distinct cases: a write past triage, a non-session actor, a failed advice walk, and a failed or timed-out claim walk. Every reader compares it `=== true`.

The same predicate carries two failure policies, and they differ because what sits beside them differs: on the claim path a failure costs the field and the claim stands; on the advice path a failure costs the field and the rest of the advice stands.
